newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen end slightly lower after quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen end slightly lower after quiet trade.

text.p: The key December three-month Euroyen interest rate futures ended down slightly on Monday but rose from their earlier lows on short-covering.
The topside remained somewhat heavy after a senior MOF official was quoted as telling Le Monde last week that a rise in Japan's discount rate was expected in the coming year.
The December contract ended at 98.90 after moving between 98.87 and 98.90. Turnover was 29,972 contracts.

Senior MOF official Eisuke Sakakibara was quoted as saying that a 0.50 percentage point interest rate rise would still leave Japan's discount rate at a low level and such a move should be expected from the Bank of Japan in the coming year.

These comments prompted selling overseas on Friday and took the key contract lower by Tokyo midday. "But as what he said was in line with what many in the market are thinking, some short-covering emerged in afternoon trade," a long-term credit bank trader said.
Activity was otherwise quiet as the market took a wait-and-see stance ahead of key economic data later this week.
